questions.prompt: What is the main difference between a meteor and a meteorite?
options: A meteorite is larger than a meteor.
A meteor burns up in the atmosphere; a meteorite hits the ground.
A meteor is made of ice; a meteorite is made of rock.
There is no difference; they are interchangeable terms.
questions.note: A meteor is the visible streak in the atmosphere. If part of the object reaches the surface, it is a meteorite.

questions.prompt: Where is the main asteroid belt located in our solar system?
questions.note: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

questions.prompt: The NASA mission OSIRIS-REx successfully returned a sample from which near-Earth asteroid?
questions.note: OSIRIS-REx collected and returned a sample from asteroid Bennu.

questions.prompt: In astronomical terms, what classifies as a Near-Earth Object (NEO)?
options: A comet or asteroid whose orbit brings it into Earth's neighborhood
Space debris left in Low Earth Orbit
Stars located within 10 light-years of Earth
questions.note: NEOs are comets or asteroids with orbits that approach Earth's orbital region.

questions.prompt: Which direction does a comet's tail always point?
questions.note: Solar wind and radiation pressure push comet tails away from the Sun.

questions.prompt: The scientific field of "Astrometry" is specifically focused on:
options: The precise measurement of positions and movements of celestial bodies
The study of atmospheric weather on other planets
questions.note: Astrometry deals with accurate positions, distances, and motions of celestial objects.

questions.prompt: What was the first spacecraft to successfully land a probe on a comet?
questions.note: ESA's Rosetta mission deployed the Philae lander onto comet 67P.

questions.prompt: What is the largest object in the main asteroid belt, also classified as a dwarf planet?
questions.note: Ceres is the largest body in the main belt and is classified as a dwarf planet.

questions.prompt: What scale is used to measure the brightness of celestial objects as seen from Earth?
questions.note: Apparent magnitude describes how bright an object appears from Earth.
